hints: The order alternates between the start and the end. If the back half were reversed, how would the two halves combine?
Three classic list moves: find the middle (fast/slow), reverse the second half in place, then weave the two halves together one node from each.

1. Find the middle: slow and fast start at head; move while fast.next and fast.next.next exist.
  2. Cut: second = slow.next, slow.next = null; reverse second.
  3. Weave: with p on the first half and q on the reversed half, save both nexts, set p.next = q and q.next = savedP, advance.
  4. Return head.

approaches.name: Store nodes in an array
approaches.idea: Put node references in an array and relink with two indexes from both ends.

approaches.name: Optimal: middle, reverse, weave
approaches.idea: All in place with pointer moves.

explain: For 10→20→30→40→50 the first half is 10→20→30 and the second half 40→50 reverses to 50→40. Weaving gives 10→50→20→40→30. When the length is odd, the first half keeps the extra (middle) node, which correctly ends up last. Cutting the first half with slow.next = null prevents a cycle at the end.
recognize: Interleave nodes from the front and the back of a list → middle + reverse second half + merge alternately.
python:
class Solution:
    def reorderList(self, head: Optional[ListNode]) -> Optional[ListNode]:
        s = f = head
        while f and f.next: s, f = s.next, f.next.next
        prev, c = None, s.next; s.next = None
        while c: c.next, prev, c = prev, c, c.next
        a, b = head, prev
        while b:
            an, bn = a.next, b.next
            a.next = b; b.next = an; a, b = an, bn
        return head
javascript: function reorderList(head) { const a = []; for (let c = head; c; c = c.next) a.push(c); const b = []; for (let i = 0, j = a.length - 1; i <= j; i++, j--) { b.push(a[i]); if (i !== j) b.push(a[j]); } for (let i = 0; i < b.length; i++) b[i].next = b[i+1] || null; return b[0]; }
